name: CFO DTC Soft Reset
description: Executes a soft reset of the CFODTC by setting the reset bit (31) to true on the CFO DTC Control Register (0x9100). This bit clear counters and FIFOs; it does not change select/control bits, it does not reset the primary CFODTC Timing Interface block.

name: CFO DTC Hard Reset
description: Executes a soft reset of the CFODTC by setting the reset bit (0) to true on the CFO DTC Control Register (0x9100). This bit is like a ‘factory reset’ - it DOES change select/control/threshold bits back to defaults; it DOES reset the primary FPGA Timing Interface block. It also executes a soft reset of the CFODTC after the hard reset.

name: Flash LEDs
description: Flashes the LEDs, for example to help find the target FPGA in a multi-FPGA deployment.

name: Get Status
description: Reads and displays all registers in a human-readable format.

name: Get Simple Status
description: Similar to Get Status, this FE Macro fetches data from a select few registers. Registers DTC Control, ROC Emulation Enable, Link Enable, SERDES Reset, and SERDES Reset Done are displayed in a human-readable format.

name: Check Firefly Temperature
description: Check the temperature from the Firefly RX IIC Bus.

name: Check Firefly Loss-of-Light
description: Checking the Loss-of-Light reads from the I2C bus register on the Firefly for any light source.

name: Check FPGA Temperature
description: Get the temperature of the FPGA in degrees Celsius. A -273.0 reading is equivalent to 0x0 from the ADC on-die sensor.

name: Jitter Attenuator Setup
inputs: Source Clock (0 is from CFO, 1 is from RJ45)
description: Select the source of the jitter attenuator: a local oscilator on the DTC or the RTF. The RTF (RJ45 Timing Fanout) is a separate board to alleviate jitter accumulation. Not all DTCs are connected to the RTF.

name: Get Device Index
description: Returns the PCIe device index for this CFO/DTC instance.

name: Get Firmware Version
description: Get RTF firmware version.

name: Get Pulse Period
description: Returns the clock period of the pulse trigger in microseconds. The 'Low Pulse Width' is the number of clock cycles the trigger stays low. The amount of time the pulse is high is hard coded in firmware (10 clock cycles).

name: Get Manual Mode
description: Reads the mode of the pulse generator. When mode = 1, the RTF pauses all pulses. When mode = 0, the RTF runs continuous pulses.

name: Set Manual Mode
description: Sets the mode of the pulse generator. When mode = 1, the RTF pauses all pulses. When mode = 0, the RTF runs continuous pulses.

name: Set Burst Mode
description: Creates a burst of pulses. The RTF stops all pulses after the last count. Set manual mode to 0 to run continous pulses.

name: Set Pulse Period
inputs: Trigger Period (s, ms, us, ns, and clocks allowed) [clocks := 10ns]
description: Sets the pulse generator’s trigger period.

name: CFO Reset
description: Executes a soft reset of the CFO by setting the reset bit (31) to true on the CFO Control Register (0x9100).

name: Clock Marker Enable/Disable
description: Enable or Disable the Mu2e Clock Marker broadcast over the CFO timing links.

name: CFO Halt
description: Transitions the state machine to Halt by setting the Enable Beam Off Mode Register to off.

name: CFO Write
description: This FE Macro writes to the CFO registers.

name: Loopback Test
description: Similar to Test Loopback marker, this FE Macro repeatedly measures the delay of markers from ROCs for a specified link. The average delay is returned given the number of iterations (loopbacks), link, and delay (sleep between iterations). This FE Macro is useful for Event Window synchronization. Constraints: \t-Loopback must be less than 10,000.

name: CFO Read
description: Read from the CFO Memory Map.  Parameters: \taddress (uint16_t): Address in Memory Map.

name: Reset Runplan
description: Resets the Event Building run plan by setting the reset bit (27) to true on the CFO Control Register.

name: Compile Runplan

Default text run plan: srcs/mu2e-pcie-utils/cfoInterfaceLib/Command.txt Default binary run plan: srcs/mu2e-pcie-utils/cfoInterfaceLib/Command.bin

name: Shared Run Plan Start
inputs: Run Plan Event Window Duration (s, ms, us, ns, and clocks allowed) [clocks := 25ns] (Default = 1.8 us)
description:
This FE Macro starts the shared CFO Run Plan, with a specified Event Mode, initial Event Window Tag, and Fixed-width Window Duration or Super-cycle Emulation Event Window Duration.

Note on Event Window Duration: Remember this is a Shared Run Plan, so choose an Event Window Duration that works for all currentyl active subsystems. For example, if you are testing with the CRV and you want to emulate super cycles while the CRV takes 100us windows at 50% Duty Cycle, then choose 1.8us because this is the common denominator (i.e. both run type needs can be assembled from 1.8 us Event Window building blocks).

Example continued: The next step after starting with the common building block of 1.8 us windows, would be for you to select Shared Run Plan Join and specify your Subsystem and that you want Supercycle Emulation, while the CRV team selects Shared Run Plan Join and specifies their Subsystem and that they want 100 us windows at 50% duty cycle.

name: Shared Run Plan Stop
description: This FE Macro stops the Shared CFO Run Plan. Note this stops the Shared Run Plan for everyone! Be sure you do not want to do this! If you only want to stop for your subsystem (and not for everyone), then choose Shared Run Plan Leave, not Stop

name: Shared Run Plan Join
inputs: Subsystem Name (CRV, Calo, Tracker, STM, ExtMon, Default = Custom)
Duty Cycle (% or M:N on:event ratio, Default = 100%)
description:
This FE Macro joins the Shared CFO Run Plan with the specified subsystem and duty cycle.

Regarding Duty Cycle% specifies the duty cycle percentage of active Event Windows. M:N ratio specifies M Event Windows active every N Event Windows. For example, 40% duty cycle or 2:5 ratio with 100 us windows would be two consecutive 100 us windows active every 500 us (i.e. 2 in 5 windows active).

Here are the corresponding Subsystem Mode Bits from docdb 4914:

Tracker := bit
Calo := bit
CRV := bit
STM := bit
ExtMon (TEM) := bit
HWDev := bit

Delivery Ring RF-0 Marker TDC [15:8] Resrv’d (TEM) [7:6] (STM) [5:4] Subrun Handling [3:1] On-spill Flag [0]/Shared Run Plan Single-shot JoinSubsystem Name (CRV, Calo, Tracker, STM, ExtMon, Default = Custom)Duty Cycle (% or M:N on:event ratio, Default = 100%)Custom Mode Bit Position (0-47, Default = 0)Custom Mode Bit Count (1-48, Default = 48)Custom Mode Bit Value (Default = 0)Single-shot Event Count (Any count allowed, executed in chunks of 1-/)Result*This FE Macro joins the Shared CFO Run Plan for a single-shot (one-time) quantity of events using the OR_SINGLESHOT opcode (opcode 111). Unlike the regular Shared Run Plan Join, OR_SINGLESHOT fires only once in hardware, so the specified subsystem bit(s) are set for exactly the requested count of events and then permanently cleared by the corresponding AND mask.

Duty Cycle supports the same syntax as Shared Run Plan Join: either a percentage or M:N ratio. For single-shot, however, the resolved N in any M:N ratio is limited to N ≤ , so very coarse ratios (e.g., 1:200) are not allowed. This determines how many events are set per fine-loop pass before software batches additional passes.

Single-shot Event Count can be any count but will be built out of batches of /.

For example, if 143 events are requested you will get a batch of 100 and 43 (each batch managed by software).

name: ROC Setup
inputs: Target ROC or Mask (Default = -1 := all ROCs, or 0x111111 := all)
ROC Emulation Type (Default = 0: Internal, 1: Fiber-Loopback, 2: External)
ROC generated Data Payload fragment packet count (11-bits, Default := 16)
Block Null Heartbeats to ALL ROCs (Default := false)
Resequence Non-null Events for ALL ROCs (Default := false)
Set Auto-Gen DRP per ROC (Default := false)
description: Use this to control the parameters of the ROC Emulation of the DTC. Internal ROC emulation does not require any fibers; the ROC is emulated without using the link SERDES rx/tx. Fiber-Loopback ROC emulation requires a single fiber connected between the link SERDES rx <==> tx channels. External ROC emulation uses the link SERDES rx/tx as though it is a ROC; this means the rx/tx channels could be connected to another DTC, and the other DTC would communicate to this emulated ROC following the ROC protocol of docdb-4914.  Note: Internal and External ROC emulation can co-exist on the same DTC link. While Fiber-Loopback ROC emulation is exclusive to the other two types and will take precedence.  Auto-Gen DRP per ROC: When enabled, the DTC generates Data Request Packets automatically per-ROC (bits [21:16] of register 0x9114). The global Autogenerate DRP bit (register 0x9100 bit 23) is automatically cleared when per-ROC mode is enabled, as the global override must be off for per-ROC control to take effect.

description: Set the Event Mode Required Mask used for Event Mode filtering. A mask bit of 1 requires the corresponding Event Mode bit to also be 1.

description: Readback the current DTC Event Mode Required Mask used for CFO Event Mode filtering.

name: Loss-of-Lock Counter Read
description: Displays the number of times the CFO Control Link lost CDR lock since the last reset. Use the FE Macro Reset Loss-of-Lock Counter to reset the register counter to zero.

name: Loss-of-Lock Counter Reset
description: Use this FE Macro to reset the Loss-of-Lock register counter to zero. Resetting the DTC will also reset this register.

name: Spy Buffer
description: Dump the current DAQ DMA C2S buffers to the log (mu2edev::spy with once|wide|stacktrace flags), then issue a DTC SoftReset. Useful for diagnosing parser desync — captures whatever is sitting in the DMA buffers right now and resets the DTC so subsequent reads start clean.

name: Release All Data DMA Buffers
description: Release all currently-held DAQ DMA buffers back to the driver (getDTC()->ReleaseAllBuffers(DTC_DMA_Engine_DAQ)).

name: Get DTC Counters
description: Fetches data from all the counter registers in a human-readable format. Counters include the number of bytes and packets transmitted and received over ROC/CFO links since the last reset. Also includes Event Builder, Jitter Attenuator, Emulated ROC delay, Heartbeat packet and Data Header packet counters since last reset.

name: Get Link Lock Status
description: Read the SERDES CDR Lock bit on all links.

name: Configure DTC for HWDevmode
outputs: Setting the CFO emulated, DCS enabled and the retransmission off
description: This FE Macro prepares the DTC for HW Dev Mode (emulated CFO).

name: Read Rx Diag FIFO
description: This FE Macro reads the ROC link RX diagnostic FIFO buffer from the SERDES. When empty, the FIFO reports 0XDEADDEAD. Note: the FIFO must be read at least once before valid data appears. Reading the FIFO pulses the Read Enable input.

name: Read Tx Diag FIFO
description: This FE Macro reads the ROC link TX diagnostic FIFO buffer from the SERDES. When empty, the FIFO reports 0XDEADDEAD. Note: the FIFO must be read at least once before valid data appears. Reading the FIFO pulses the Read Enable input.

name: Get Link Errors
description: This FE Macro returns the number of errors on all links since last reset. Errors include the number of times illegal characters, a disparity, PRBS, and CRC error the SERDES has received. It also includes the number of EVB RX packet errors, and number of times the Jitter Attenuator lost the RX Recovered clock and lost the RX External clock since last reset.

name: Loopback CFO Emulator Test Run
description: Executes a loopback test at the DTC's CFO emulator, and broadcasts loopback markers to all ROCs.

name: Loopback CFO Emulator Multi Test Run
description: Executes many loopback tests at the DTC's CFO emulator, and broadcasts loopback markers to all ROCs, and returns the average result.

name: Loopback Manual Setup
description: Toggles the DTC CFO loopback mode. If setAsPassthrough is enabled, CFO loopback is disabled and CFO markers will be transmitted to the next DTC (Normal operation). If setAsPassthrough is disabled, CFO loopback is enabled and the CFO Link SERDES output is routed back to the source. The loopback functionality is managed through the DTC Control Register bit 28.
